actors.name: MP Materials
actors.role: mines Mountain Pass, the only US rare-earth mine, and is building magnets

triad.execution: Price floor and offtake underwrite its magnet plant
triad.environment: Sits inside a US-China export-control dispute

actors.advantage: The US Department of Defense is its largest-shareholder-in-waiting and guarantees $110/kg NdPr for 10 years, so a state removes its price risk. China listed it on its export-control list in June 2026.
actors.desire: Become the non-Chinese magnet supply chain.
actors.fear: China floods the market or cuts it off from inputs; the floor depends on Congress.

actors.name: Freeport-McMoRan
actors.role: largest listed copper miner outside state firms; owns Grasberg
actors.advantage: Copper is the wire of every data centre and grid; Grasberg is about 3% of world supply and its outage tightened the whole market.
actors.desire: Restore Grasberg and sell into the AI build-out.

actors.name: Shin-Etsu Chemical
actors.advantage: Shin-Etsu holds about 28% of world silicon wafers, the largest share, ahead of SUMCO's 25% and GlobalWafers' 15% (single-report estimate); its market cap is $61.01 billion.
actors.fear: Chinese wafer entrants and weak demand.

actors.name: GlobalWafers
actors.role: Taiwan's wafer maker, third in the global wafer ranks
actors.advantage: A non-Japanese wafer source near the fabs.

actors.name: Kazatomprom
actors.role: Kazakhstan's uranium miner; Kazakhstan mined 39% of world uranium in 2024
actors.advantage: Kazatomprom mined 12,463 tonnes of uranium in 2024, 21% of the world, ahead of Cameco (17%) and Orano (11%). Kazakhstan as a country mined 39%, nearly double its own output share, because Uranium One and Kazatomprom's joint ventures also work there.

actors.name: Cameco
actors.role: Canadian uranium miner and fuel services
actors.advantage: Canada mined 24% of world uranium in 2024.

actors.name: Air Liquide
actors.role: supplier of the gases fabs consume (nitrogen, argon, helium and others)
actors.advantage: On-site gas plants at fabs create switching costs.

actors.name: China
actors.role: controls most rare-earth refining, magnets, gallium and silicon production
actors.advantage: China holds over 90% of magnet rare-earth refining, nearly 95% of magnets, 99% of primary low-purity gallium and about 80% of silicon materials, refines about 48% of the world's copper, and licenses exports as a weapon; the October 2025 rare-earth controls are suspended only to 10 November 2026. It also set up a 344 billion yuan chip fund (Big Fund III) in May 2024.
actors.desire: Hold chokepoints as leverage while building its own chips.
actors.fear: Loss of access to Western tools and chips.

actors.name: United States government
actors.advantage: The US government owns 9.9% of Intel, guarantees MP Materials a price floor, taxes some AI chip imports, and licenses what NVIDIA may sell to China, taking a share of the revenue. CHIPS Act awards of $6.6bn (TSMC), $6.165bn (Micron) and about $4.75bn (Samsung) were finalized in late 2024.

actors.name: Japan
actors.role: funds Rapidus and hosts the wafer makers
actors.advantage: Public money builds a domestic 2nm foundry (Rapidus: IPA put in 250 billion yen, 100 billion plus 150 billion, in 2026) and pays 732 billion yen for TSMC's second Kumamoto fab.

actors.name: European Union
actors.advantage: A smaller programme than the US.

actors.name: Netherlands
actors.role: licenses ASML's lithography exports; since September 2024 it, not the US, licenses ASML's 1970i and 1980i DUV systems
actors.advantage: Used the Goods Availability Act, then suspended the order.

actors.name: Taiwan
actors.role: hosts TSMC, holds 6.38% of it, and decides which TSMC process may be built abroad

triad.information: TSMC's process know-how stays on the island under the N-1 rule
triad.execution: The National Development Fund is TSMC's second-largest holder; the state sets the export rule
triad.environment: Hosts the foundry that held 72.5% of top-10 foundry revenue in Q2 2026

actors.advantage: Taiwan's state is a 6.38% shareholder of TSMC and writes the N-1 rule that lets only a process one generation older leave the island. That makes the world's AI chip supply depend on Taiwan's own law. A January 2026 deal with Washington cut US tariffs on most Taiwanese goods from 20% to 15% against US$250 billion of Taiwanese investment pledges.
actors.desire: Keep the newest node at home while buying US protection with fabs in Arizona.
actors.fear: China taking the island, or a US tariff of 100% on chips if Taiwan does not build in America.

actors.name: Rapidus
actors.role: state-backed Japanese start-up building a 2nm foundry

triad.information: Seeks leading-edge process know-how through partners
triad.execution: Capital from the state agency IPA and 32 private companies
triad.environment: Japan's METI plan for domestic leading-edge supply

actors.advantage: Rapidus has no market share yet; its position is public money. The state agency IPA put in 100 billion yen and then 150 billion yen in 2026, and 32 companies put in 167.6 billion yen. Total funding is 424.95 billion yen, cumulative.
actors.fear: Failing to reach volume while the state's patience runs out.

actors.name: ESMC (Dresden)
actors.role: TSMC-led joint venture with Bosch, Infineon and NXP building a fab in Dresden

triad.environment: EUR 5bn German state aid approved by the Commission

actors.advantage: A fab that exists because of state aid: the Commission approved EUR 5 billion in August 2024, the biggest award under the EU Chips Act at the time.
actors.desire: Bring a TSMC fab to Europe.

actors.name: SUMCO

triad.environment: Sits in Japan beside the chip fabs it supplies

actors.advantage: SUMCO holds about 25% of world silicon wafers, second to Shin-Etsu's 28%, in a market where five firms hold about 91% (single-report estimate).
actors.desire: Sell more 300mm wafers into the AI memory and logic upturn.
actors.fear: Chinese wafer makers and a cyclical downturn.

flashpoints.title: China licenses rare earths
flashpoints.mechanism: Export licences on seven, then twelve, rare earths turn processing share into leverage.
flashpoints.outcome: Suspended in Nov 2025 to 10 Nov 2026; April licensing remains.

flashpoints.title: Pentagon underwrites MP Materials
flashpoints.mechanism: A $110/kg floor removes the price risk that Chinese pricing imposed.
flashpoints.outcome: China listed MP Materials on its export-control list in June 2026.

flashpoints.title: State becomes Intel's shareholder
flashpoints.mechanism: Unpaid grants were converted into 9.9% of Intel.

flashpoints.title: H20 licence rule
flashpoints.mechanism: A licence requirement stranded H20 inventory. A deal reported in August 2025 gave the government 15% of Nvidia and AMD China revenue; Trump later said 25% for H200.
flashpoints.outcome: NVIDIA booked a $4.5bn charge in Q1 FY2026 (guided at about $5.5bn); China's customs then blocked H200 imports and NVIDIA's China share fell to zero.

flashpoints.title: Taiwan keeps TSMC's newest node at home
flashpoints.mechanism: The N-1 rule lets only a process one generation older leave the island, so even TSMC's US fabs trail Taiwan.
flashpoints.outcome: A January 2026 deal cut US tariffs on most Taiwanese goods to 15% against US$250bn of pledged investment.

flashpoints.title: China's gallium ban on the US
flashpoints.mechanism: One country makes 99% of primary low-purity gallium, so a ban on exports to the US bites at once.
flashpoints.outcome: China lifted the ban for one year in November 2025; the related ban is suspended to 27 November 2026.

flashpoints.title: The Netherlands licenses ASML's DUV tools
flashpoints.mechanism: From 7 September 2024 ASML needs a Dutch licence, not a US one, to ship the 1970i and 1980i to China.
flashpoints.outcome: Control over the exports passed from Washington to The Hague.

flashpoints.title: Japan buys a 2nm foundry with state money
flashpoints.mechanism: The IPA put 100 billion yen and then 150 billion yen into Rapidus, beside 167.6 billion yen from 32 firms.
flashpoints.outcome: Cumulative funding is 424.95 billion yen; about 59% is state-agency capital and 40% private.

notes: Second pass. Unverified, left out: germanium's world production share (USGS says data are limited; a 68% figure from Asian Metal/Guangxi Yusheng and S&P's 90% refining figure could not be read by the gate); Taiwan's share of advanced packaging and of leading-edge logic capacity (no readable 2025-26 source); BHP and Codelco copper shares (Engineering News paywalled); Siltronic and SK Siltron wafer shares beyond the single-report figures; the Dutch 2025-26 ASML licence changes; the stakes held by China's Big Fund III (sources disagree: China Development Bank 17.4% per The Register, Ministry of Finance 17% per others); Bloomberg's 476bn yen for Kumamoto fab 1. Wafer shares come from one secondary report (faxiangongchang, citing SEMI for market size) and are flagged as such. The 59%/40% Rapidus split is a calculation: 250bn and 167.6bn of 424.95bn yen. MGX stakes in OpenAI and Anthropic rounds: see earlier-round facts owners-openai-round-2026-leads and str-anthropic-series-g; no amount for MGX alone is verified.
